situation: A large wall calendar hangs on a wall as a neat grid of twelve equal pages, in four columns and three rows, each page showing a different small picture and background colour that matches its season: snowmen, snowdrops, spring blossom, rain, summer beach, sunflowers, harvest apples, falling leaves, mushrooms, first frost, and a Christmas tree. No numbers or letters appear on any page.

prompt: A large wall calendar hangs on a wall as a neat grid of twelve equal pages, in four columns and three rows, each page showing a different small picture and background colour that matches its season: snowmen, snowdrops, spring blossom, rain, summer beach, sunflowers, harvest apples, falling leaves, mushrooms, first frost, and a Christmas tree. No numbers or letters appear on any page. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
